messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: abnormal KV cache growth + continuous-batching latency spike detected on svc-inference-prod us-west-2. Error rate up 6% and tail p99 token latency +3.2x. Pager -> @erin_oncall.

erin_oncall: I’m on it, looking at dashboards now. Noting big growth in cache entries and packer queue length.

mike_sre: seeing mixed workload patterns — lots of short chat requests interleaved with long completion streams. Batcher is favoring long requests and starving short ones -> thin-queue backpressure.

lucas_ml: that matches a rollout from yesterday: continuous-batching change to aggressively pack similar shapes (pack-size=32 default). Might have changed heuristics for mixed-shape workloads.

eng_runtime: rolling config can be toggled. Reverting packer default to legacy=pack-size=8 is quick; does that sound safe?

erin_oncall: do it. We need to reduce KV cache blowup too — prefetch is over-aggressive and filling memory because long requests keep KV open. Throttle prefetch to 0.5x.

eng_runtime: ack, planning a staged config change: set pack-size=8, prefetch-factor=0.5 across us-west-2 region. Rolling to 10% canary -> 50% -> 100%.

deploy-bot: deploy started: config/packer@canary-1 -> pack-size=8, prefetch-factor=0.5 (10% hosts).

customer_ops: heads-up — we have two paying enterprise customers on this region; they might see intermittent tail latency. Any ETA on mitigation?

erin_oncall: initial canary in. Monitoring error rate and p99.

mike_sre: quick snapshot: before change: p99 token latency 820ms, error rate 6.3%, avg KV entries per host 1.8M. After canary (10%): canary hosts p99 -> 240ms, error rate 0.9%, KV entries -45% on canary.

lucas_ml: that’s promising. If we ramp, we should watch for pack utilization regressions for long-only customers. Might need a compensation rule: long-only requests can use pack-size=32 explicitly via route override.

erin_oncall: agree. Continue ramp to 50% then 100% if stable for 5m. Also reducing per-route default batching timeout from 80ms -> 30ms to favor short requests.

eng_runtime: ramp to 50% in progress.

deploy-bot: deploy progress: canary-2 -> 50% hosts; expected finish ~3m.

mike_sre: metrics after 50%: global p99 down to 360ms, global error rate 1.6%, KV entries trending down but not yet stable. Pack backlog reduced by ~60% across hosts in the roll.

customer_ops: pinged the two customers, they say some requests were slow but no customer-reported errors yet.

erin_oncall: continue to 100%. If spike returns after full roll, fallback plan B: enable paging throttle (kv_paging_threshold=0.7) to force eviction.

eng_runtime: rolling to 100% now.

deploy-bot: deploy complete: config applied to 100% of us-west-2.

mike_sre: post-roll numbers: p99 210ms, error rate 0.6%, KV entries per host ~420k (down 76% from peak). Prefetch ops down 68%.

lucas_ml: we've mitigated the immediate blowup. However, we still see tail spikes intermittently when long requests cluster with short spikes — scheduler fairness issue remains latent.

erin_oncall: open a follow-up runbook task: add per-route shaping and implement adaptive pack windows. Also add a temporal isolation policy: when a long request queue > X then temporarily reduce pack-size for that pod.

mike_sre: noted. Creating GH issue & triage item.

eng_runtime: we should also add a targeted canary for mixed-shape workloads (synthetic mix test). I can add a periodic job to exercise that.

customer_ops: will keep monitoring customers and escalate if anything observed. We flagged post-incident note for both enterprise contacts.

tara_prod: quick question — did the revert affect throughput for large-generation customers? Any regression?

mike_sre: throughput for long-only routes down ~4% but within SLA. We can add an explicit route override to keep high pack-size for customers who need throughput.

lucas_ml: short-term action list: 1) keep current config 24h, 2) add per-route overrides to keep pack-size high for long-only routes, 3) ship adaptive packer heuristic in 3 sprints, 4) add synthetic mixed-shape job to load tests.

erin_oncall: handoff: I’ll keep monitoring for 1 hour, then hand to EU morning oncall @mike_sre for day watch. Create H1 incident summary and customer impact note.

mike_sre: taking day watch after erin. I’ll add expanded tracing on packer decisions and KV cache evictions.

deploy-bot: rollback/rollback-check not required — config change is stable.

incident-bot: Incident update: Mitigated. Severity downgraded to SEV3. Root cause likely continuous-batching heuristic + aggressive prefetch exposing packer starvation for mixed-shape workloads. Postmortem required.

erin_oncall: filing postmortem stub now with incident timeline, initial metrics, config diffs, and action items. Will include customer impact section and planned mitigations.

customer_ops: thanks. I’ll prepare customer-friendly blurb for the two affected enterprise customers and start collecting any logs they can share.

erin_oncall: handoff complete at 1823462100. Leaving notes in the incident doc and assigning follow-ups: ENG-RUNTIME: adaptive-packer (P0-> P1), ENG-ML: eval mixed-shape test, SRE: monitoring alerts for packer-saturation, CUSTOMER-OPS: customer comms.

mike_sre: acknowledged. If anything spikes during the day watch I’ll reopen and notify the oncall rotation.

lucas_ml: thanks everyone. Adding a short eval today to ensure quality doesn’t regress with lower pack-size for long routes.

incident-bot: Incident closed? (manual close required)

erin_oncall: closing the alert channel now — will convert this thread into a postmortem draft.
